Record first quarter - revenue $355.7M up 37% YoY, strong 'especially after growing at triple-digit for the past three consecutive years.'
Celsius alone drove ~47% of total energy-category growth; reached an 11.5% MULOC share (a full point above Q4 2023, ~4 points above prior year).
Record gross margin of 51.2% (up from 43.8%) on reduced freight and raw-material costs; adjusted EBITDA up 81% to ~$88M; net income up 106% to $65M.

Central headwind: inventory movements by largest customer PepsiCo (~62% of Q1 NA revenue) - Q1 revenue would have been higher absent these; YoY variation due to elevated Q1 2023 restocking that did not repeat. Management told analysts not to 'bake in a reversal.'
Watch items: rising fuel and aluminum costs (aluminum largely locked in around Q4), cost of a new March Pepsi incentive program, and higher promotional period entering '100 days of summer.'
Spring shelf resets ~one-third complete at quarter-end, expected fully done by end of June - 'best shelf space gains in company history,' with full scanner-data effect from July.
New March PepsiCo incentive program aligns shared priorities toward becoming the #1 global energy brand; ramps over first 6-8 months, 'cruising' by the back half, with an associated cost.
Celsius Essentials (16-oz) reached 54.5% ACV by mid-April (a 5.5-point share increase since February); new 12-oz flavors (Galaxy Vibe, Blue Razz Lemonade, Sparkling Raspberry Peach, Astro Vibe).
Margin guidance deliberately conservative - reiterated February 'high 40s' framework, declining to lock into the 50s despite the 51.2% print.
International: UK/Ireland live as of April; Australia, New Zealand, France planned to begin gradually in Q4 2024 with phased 2025 expansion; Canada (launched January) reached 5.5% share.
Faster shipment cycles (seven days vs prior ~14) will impact revenue-recognition timing relative to depletions.
Sales and key-accounts team grew ~85% YTD; 3x sales staff planned by year-end versus prior year.

Asked how Q2 has progressed on consumption, whether inventories are now tight/low into more resets, whether some of the ~$20M reverses in Q2; and whether the margin beat contained one-time items or was pure leverage.

CEO Fieldly said Celsius does not control PepsiCo inventory but believes everyone is optimizing; Celsius itself optimized inventory ~$47M over 15 months. CFO Langhans said depletions are 'rock-solid' but April is 'a new normal' and explicitly 'I wouldn't bake in a reversal.' On margins: favorable Q1 freight (fluctuates quarter to quarter, depends on back-half fuel) and raw-material leverage, but with 100-days-of-summer promotional intensity rising, would not 'put the line in the sand' at the Q1 rate - sticking with the 'high 40s' framework for Q2-Q4.
Under-Shipment vs. End Demand & Service Levels

Said rough math implies Celsius under-shipped demand per scanner data for two quarters; asked what management says to the visible gap, and whether PepsiCo's shelf management has affected out-of-stocks/service levels.

Fieldly said PepsiCo is at 'really good inventory levels,' Celsius is maintaining deliveries and keeping product in stock, scan data is strong, and the company just broke a record at 11.5% share - product is flowing. Both sides are learning each other's supply chains. No out-of-stocks beyond normal course. Langhans aligned - no service issues as PepsiCo optimizes.
Markets Near 15% Share, Spring Resets & Coolers
Asked for color on markets near a 15% share and what was done; where spring-reset gains are most significant (SKUs, facings, shelf quality); and the 2024 cooler plan including non-Celsius coolers.

Fieldly said Celsius is in 12 major US metros above 15% share with several others approaching, driven by deeper Pepsi collaboration, larger teams and a methodical activation approach. Convenience is the biggest reset opportunity (e.g., the Publix move from HPC into the energy set with front-checkout coolers); full resets expected done by end of June. Declined to give a cooler number but said a 'substantial' number is planned; ~3,000 coolers placed in Q1.
Aluminum Exposure, Pepsi Incentive Margin Impact & Costco/Food Service
Asked the magnitude of COGS exposure to aluminum and timing; what the Pepsi agreement amendment means for margin; and the drivers of the sequential Costco decline and flat food service.

CFO Langhans clarified his earlier April comment referred only to days-on-hand being consistent March-into-April. Celsius has locked in a lot of its aluminum pricing (typically around Q4), so it is in good shape despite rising fuel. The Pepsi incentive program is incentive-based with an associated cost, ramping over the first 6-8 months and 'cruising' by the back half. Costco/club softness reflects a strong Q4 Thanksgiving/Black Friday bump and Q1 club seasonality; food service remains strong (~12% is good).
Shelf-Reset Phasing, Destocking Floor & Incentive-Program Rationale

Keypour asked whether further TDP/average-items movement implies new flavors/innovation or double/triple facing. Lavery asked whether to expect more destocking (how low could it go) and the rationale for the Pepsi incentive program given existing strong momentum.

Fieldly said the reset goal is double/triple facing and secondary/better placements (which may not lift average items per store in scanner data), citing the Publix HPC-to-energy-aisle transition; innovation also launching (Essentials, Galaxy Vibe). On destocking, Celsius cannot control it - sales flowing strongly at the register, balancing appears finalized, things seem 'somewhat stable' exiting March. On the incentive program, framed as standard practice that further aligns priorities within PEP Energy; Langhans added it is about full alignment to go after the #1 and #2 players.

Asked how much of Celsius's ~half of category growth is new consumers versus buy-rate through new occasions, and household penetration/repeat performance; and what is being done differently in the 31 drill-deep markets and expected share results.

Fieldly said growth is largely incremental, not brand-shifting: latest data showed ~35% intensification (core consumers consuming more), ~42% new-to-category, ~23% brand shift. Celsius is expanding the category, aided by the Pepsi partnership (Jersey Mike's, Dunkin'), better-for-you attributes and the fitness trend. Household penetration reached an all-time high of 29.7%. Declined to detail drill-deep market strategies (competitors listening) - a proprietary approach starting with the employee and a great product, touching consumers where they live, work and play.
Year-Ago Inventory Comp & Reset Phasing/Share Outlook

Asked the CFO to remind investors what the inventory dynamic is comping against and whether the scanner-data gap continues or aligns through the year; and on resets, when the one-third occurred in Q1, whether the steady 11.5% share reflects a benefit, the phasing of benefits, and whether reset track growth/share can be contextualized.

CFO Langhans said Celsius was just getting started with PepsiCo last year. Q1 2023 saw ~$25M of inventory buildup, minor buildup across Q2/Q3 then steady through Q4 (some innovation pipe-fill). Q1 2024 saw clear optimization. No product-on-shelf issues; April days-on-hand maintained at March levels. On resets, the four-week share has climbed to roughly 11.8% in the last couple of weeks, progress continues through April into May; once resets fully baked in by early July the company will see where it stands - reiterating expectations for the best space gains in company history and a 'phenomenal back half.'
